evidence_chain: MYR reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.00 billion, up $166.8 million year over year; T&D revenue was $541.0 million and C&I revenue was $459.4 million. Source: MYR Group Q1 2026 results, https://investor.myrgroup.com/node/16251

As of March 31, 2026, MYR backlog was $2.84 billion, up 7.7% year over year; T&D backlog was $980.7 million and C&I backlog was $1.86 billion. Source: MYR Group Q1 2026 results, https://investor.myrgroup.com/node/16251

MYR’s Q1 2026 investor presentation describes the company as a market leader in electrical construction, with 9,000+ employees, 65+ office locations, 90%+ repeat clients, and services spanning Transmission, Distribution, Substation, Energy Storage, Manufacturing, Data Centers, Clean Energy, and related markets. Source: SEC-filed investor presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700923/000070092326000030/myrginvestorpresentation.htm

The same investor presentation states that data centers have been an important and growing C&I end market and that new interconnections, substations, and infrastructure upgrades to data centers create opportunities for the T&D segment. Source: SEC-filed investor presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700923/000070092326000030/myrginvestorpresentation.htm

On the Q1 2026 earnings call, management cited awards including an Arizona MSA spanning transmission, distribution and substations; two greenfield substations in Texas; substation work in Arizona; a 345 kV transmission-line project in South Carolina; and other overhead transmission and distribution work. Source: Q1 2026 corrected transcript, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/e6ebdf11-b6d6-4f30-b0f0-ba45726ea9ab

On the Q1 2026 earnings call, C&I management said data-center projects and water/wastewater projects are driving the strongest growth in the construction market, and disclosed multiple data-center project awards in New Jersey, Arizona, California, and Colorado. Source: Q1 2026 corrected transcript, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/e6ebdf11-b6d6-4f30-b0f0-ba45726ea9ab

MYR’s 2025 Form 10-K shows 2025 contract revenues of $2.00 billion in T&D and $1.66 billion in C&I, with operating income margins of 7.9% and 5.9%, respectively. Source: 2025 Form 10-K, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/f15fbf6f-78c7-4fbc-801a-5638665c2d1c

MYR’s 2025 Form 10-K also highlights execution risk: 2025 T&D margins were negatively affected by labor and project inefficiencies on certain projects, and C&I margins were negatively affected by labor/project inefficiencies and unfavorable change orders. Source: 2025 Form 10-K, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/f15fbf6f-78c7-4fbc-801a-5638665c2d1c
As of June 8, 2026 around 18:30 UTC, MYRG market capitalization was approximately $6.96 billion. Source: market data retrieved via finance tool.

The evidence supports that MYRG has real exposure to data centers, substations, T&D, and interconnect-style infrastructure; however, the company has not yet provided enough granular backlog disclosure to prove that AI/data-center power infrastructure is the dominant driver.

If the electrical-construction labor and commissioning pool becomes a binding constraint for data-center and grid projects, MYRG’s execution capacity could command better backlog quality, better project selectivity, and possibly more resilient demand than generic construction peers.
falsification_plan: Falsify if future backlog growth is mostly generic commercial construction, transportation, or non-power C&I work rather than data centers, substations, T&D, utility interconnects, grid modernization, or high-voltage projects.
Falsify if backlog rises but gross margin and operating margin deteriorate because of fixed-price contracts, labor inefficiencies, unfavorable change orders, or poor project closeout.
Falsify if management stops citing data-center, substation, interconnection, or T&D awards while AI data-center and utility capex remain strong elsewhere.
Falsify if labor constraints prevent MYRG from converting backlog to revenue, causing delays, claims, or working-capital strain.
Falsify if large utilities, data-center developers, or hyperscalers appear to consolidate work away from MYRG subsidiaries toward larger EPC competitors.
Falsify if book-to-bill and backlog decline in T&D and C&I while broader grid and data-center power indicators remain strong, suggesting MYRG lacks competitive capture.
Falsify if cash conversion deteriorates materially through claims, contract assets, receivables, or disputed change orders, indicating that reported backlog quality is weaker than headline figures.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog growth, book-to-bill, margin improvement, and project awards are specifically tied to grid modernization, substations, utility interconnects, high-voltage transmission, and data-center electrical infrastructure rather than broad nonresidential construction.
next_research_tasks: Extract three-year backlog by segment from 10-Ks and 10-Qs: total backlog, T&D backlog, C&I backlog, book-to-bill, and backlog-to-forward-revenue conversion.

Build a keyword table from 2024-2026 filings and transcripts: data center, hyperscale, AI, substation, interconnect, transmission, distribution, grid modernization, MSA, fixed price, change order, labor, productivity, safety, commissioning.

Compare MYRG to reference leaders and peers in two lanes: obvious power-equipment names versus execution-layer contractors such as Quanta Services, MasTec, EMCOR, IES Holdings, and other electrical contractors. The goal is not to recommend a stock but to test relative purity of exposure and evidence quality.
Review contract mix disclosures: fixed-price, unit-price, T&E, cost-plus, reimbursable, MSAs, and whether higher data-center exposure increases or decreases risk.
Check working-capital quality each quarter: contract assets, contract liabilities, receivable days, claims, change orders, cash conversion, and free cash flow versus EBITDA.
Track labor signals: headcount, wage inflation, union/non-union mix where disclosed, subcontractor dependence, OSHA/safety metrics, TCIR, LTIR, and recruiting/training commentary.
Map announced project geographies to data-center and grid-load hotspots: Arizona, Texas, Colorado, California, New Jersey, South Carolina, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Iowa, and Canada.

Search utility commission filings, interconnection queues, local permits, and data-center development records for MYRG subsidiary names to confirm whether disclosed awards connect to large-load power infrastructure.

Monitor whether management gives more granular end-market disclosure in future investor presentations, especially percentage of C&I backlog tied to data centers and percentage of T&D backlog tied to substations/interconnections.

Create a falsification dashboard item that flags any quarter with backlog growth but margin compression, negative estimate changes, rising contract assets, or language about unfavorable change orders.
risks: Electrical construction is project-execution intensive. Labor inefficiencies, productivity misses, safety incidents, unfavorable change orders, project delays, and closeout disputes can erase the apparent benefit of strong demand.
C&I revenue growth in Q1 2026 was primarily tied to fixed-price contracts, and fixed-price exposure can pressure margins if labor, materials, subcontractor, or schedule assumptions are wrong.
Reported backlog may not map cleanly to AI/data-center power infrastructure. If backlog is dominated by lower-margin or generic construction work, the chokepoint thesis weakens.

C&I demand still includes broader commercial, transportation, manufacturing, water/wastewater, clean-energy, and other markets. A slowdown in nonresidential construction could offset strength in data centers.
The same skilled-labor scarcity that creates a potential moat can also limit revenue conversion or raise wage costs.
Large utilities, hyperscalers, or data-center developers may route work through larger EPCs, preferred vendors, or bundled equipment-and-services providers.

The 2025 Form 10-K shows both T&D and C&I margins were affected by estimate changes, labor/project inefficiencies, and change-order dynamics, confirming that the business can be volatile even in favorable demand environments.

Although the candidate is underfollowed by theme investors, the stock is no longer extremely cheap or obscure by size, with market cap around $7 billion on June 8, 2026. Any report should avoid treating underfollowed thematic exposure as a valuation conclusion.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver: AI data centers, electrification, reshoring, grid modernization, renewable interconnection, power reliability. System bottleneck: power availability and grid connection. Physical asset layer: transmission lines, distribution systems, substations, interconnects, data-center electrical rooms, energy storage, clean-energy tie-ins. Execution layer: electrical EPC, specialty electrical construction, project management, procurement coordination, skilled labor, testing, commissioning, safety and quality control. MYRG sits primarily in the execution layer across T&D and C&I, with exposure to substations, transmission, distribution, data centers, manufacturing, transportation, clean energy, and energy storage.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: MYRG 可能是 AI 数据中心与电网升级链条中的二阶卡点。市场通常先关注变压器、开关柜、电缆、燃机、核电或公用事业资产，但即便设备可得，项目仍需要合格电气施工队伍、变电站施工、T&D 升级、并网执行、采购协调、测试和调试能力才能真正落地。MYRG 的公开材料显示其业务覆盖 Transmission & Distribution、substation、data centers、clean energy、energy storage、manufacturing 等场景，并在 2026 年一季度披露了数据中心项目、变电站项目、345 kV transmission line 项目以及 record backlog。该 thesis 的关键升级点是：如果后续披露显示 backlog 与收入增长主要来自数据中心电力接入、变电站、T&D、grid modernization、utility interconnect 和高复杂度电气基础设施，而不是普通商业建筑周期，则 MYRG 的供应链位置应从“普通 specialty contractor”上调为“电力基础设施执行能力瓶颈”。
deep_reports.thesis_en: MYRG may be a second-order chokepoint in AI data-center power deployment and grid modernization. The market often focuses first on transformers, switchgear, cables, turbines, nuclear, or regulated utilities, but even when hardware is available, projects still require qualified electrical construction labor, substation construction, T&D upgrades, interconnection execution, procurement coordination, testing, and commissioning. Recent MYRG disclosures connect the company to Transmission & Distribution, substations, data centers, clean energy, energy storage, manufacturing, and large electrical construction. Q1 2026 materials also cite data-center awards, substation awards, a 345 kV transmission-line project, and record backlog. The key upgrade condition is evidence that backlog and revenue growth are specifically tied to data-center power connections, substations, T&D, grid modernization, utility interconnects, and high-complexity electrical infrastructure rather than generic commercial construction.

deep_reports.title_en: MYRG: an electrical execution bottleneck hidden behind a specialty-construction label
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: MYRG is commonly categorized as a specialty contractor or electrical construction company rather than an AI power infrastructure company. That label can cause investors screening for energy bottlenecks to focus on more obvious hardware suppliers or regulated utilities while missing the execution constraint. The hidden angle is that data-center and grid projects can be delayed not only by unavailable equipment but also by scarce qualified crews, safety-compliant execution, project sequencing, change orders, and commissioning capacity.

summary: Layer 5 mini deep report for MYR Group Inc. / MYRG. The research target remains an underfollowed small-cap candidate in the Energy and Power Chain funnel. Core hypothesis: the chokepoint may be electrical infrastructure execution capacity, not just transformers, switchgear, generation, or turbines. Evidence has improved versus the initial brief because recent company materials and Q1 2026 commentary explicitly connect MYRG to T&D, substations, transmission, data centers, interconnections, grid modernization, skilled workforce, and backlog. However, the thesis is not yet fully proven because public disclosures still do not break backlog down precisely by AI/data-center power infrastructure versus broader C&I and utility work.
